posts.title: The Price — concept reel
posts.quote: Two men were offered the same thing. One sold everything for joy. One walked away sorrowful.
posts.onscreen: Text only, no voiceover. Music cuts to silence for the turn at 0:38 and returns at 0:50.
posts.endline: The kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field, and for joy thereof he selleth all that he hath. (MATTHEW 13:44)

captions.instagram:
Two men were offered the same thing.

One found treasure in a field that wasn't his, buried it again, went home and sold everything he owned to buy that field.

The other was told to sell what he had and follow. He went away sorrowful.

Neither was told what it was worth. Both had to price it themselves.

So have you. Not in what you say about it. In what your week is arranged around.

🎬 From "Enter Into The Kingdom" — Rev Ifeayinchukwu Obi. Full sermon on YouTube (search Calvary Hephzibah).

posts.title: Church is for people who have problems?
posts.quote: You think it's for weak people. Church is for people who have problems. Is that what you think? You need to change your mind.
posts.onscreen: "Say it out loud." → "Even if your voice shakes."

captions.instagram:
There is a moment, usually a small one, where you know what you believe and you say nothing.

A conversation at work. A doctor's letter. A bill you have read three times. You hold the thing you believe quietly, in your chest, and hope it is enough.

He says something worth sitting with: what you speak into a situation changes how you stand in it. Not because words are magic, but because staying silent and intimidated keeps you intimidated.

He is not asking you to be loud. He is asking you to be honest, out loud, once.

Save this for the next time your voice shakes.

🎬 From "Enter Into The Kingdom" — Rev Ifeayinchukwu Obi. Full sermon on YouTube (search Calvary Hephzibah).

posts.title: Every decision, never for yourself
posts.quote: Every single decision you make should never be made for yourself. It should be made for Christ.
posts.onscreen: "It is not too late" → "to change your mind."

captions.instagram:
Repent is a word most people have only heard shouted.

So it has come to sound like a verdict. Like someone has already decided what you are, and the only thing left is to agree with them.

It does not mean that. It means change your mind. Think differently about who is running your life. That is the whole word.

Which is gentler than it sounds, and also more serious. Nobody can do it for you, and nobody can stop you doing it. Not your history, not what you did last week, not how long it has been.

It is not too late. It was never going to be.

🎬 From "Enter Into The Kingdom" — Rev Ifeayinchukwu Obi. Full sermon on YouTube (search Calvary Hephzibah).

posts.title: Change your mind
posts.quote: The kingdom is here. You have to change your mind. Have you changed your mind about the things of the kingdom?
posts.onscreen: "If you have thought that," → "you are not the first."

captions.instagram:
"You think it is for weak people. Church is for people who have problems."

He said that from the front, on a Sunday, to a room full of churchgoers. Not as an accusation. As a thought he knows plenty of people have had, including people sitting in front of him.

And here is the part worth noticing. He did not get defensive about it. He did not explain why it is unfair. He just asked, honestly, whether that is what you think, and then kept talking to you anyway.

If you have thought it, you are not the first, and it does not disqualify you from anything. Doubt is not the opposite of faith. It is usually the beginning of a real one.

Save this for a day you are not sure.

🎬 From "Enter Into The Kingdom" — Rev Ifeayinchukwu Obi. Full sermon on YouTube (search Calvary Hephzibah).

posts.title: Christians speak their faith
posts.quote: Christians speak their faith. If you don't speak, check yourself. That's why you are where you are.
posts.onscreen: "Not only the big ones." → "The Tuesday ones too."

captions.instagram:
Most of us quietly sort life into two piles.

The big things, which feel spiritual enough to pray about. And everything else, which is just admin. The job, the move, the diagnosis go in the first pile. How you spoke to someone on Tuesday goes in the second.

He will not let the piles stand. Every decision, he says. Not some. Not spiritual, not physical. All of them.

That sounds heavier than it is. He is not adding rules. He is saying you are not on your own in the small stuff either, and that the God you go to for the big things is already present in the ordinary ones.

What is the decision you are sitting on this week?

🎬 From "Enter Into The Kingdom" — Rev Ifeayinchukwu Obi. Full sermon on YouTube (search Calvary Hephzibah).

posts.title: Every decision, not some decisions
posts.quote: Every decision, not some decisions. Not spiritual, not physical. All decisions you take give you an opportunity to enter the kingdom.
posts.onscreen: "The life you are living" → "was never only yours."

captions.instagram:
"Every single decision you make should never be made for yourself."

Read quickly, that sounds like being erased. Like you matter less.

Sit with it a moment and it turns over. He is drawing on Paul, who said the life I now live is not mine, it is Christ living through me. Which means the weight of getting every choice right was never yours to carry alone in the first place.

Most of us are exhausted by our own decisions. Not because they are hard, but because we think everything depends on us being clever enough about them.

He is offering the opposite of that. Not less of you. Less alone.

Send this to someone who overthinks everything.

🎬 From "Enter Into The Kingdom" — Rev Ifeayinchukwu Obi. Full sermon on YouTube (search Calvary Hephzibah).

posts.title: You are the one carrying the Spirit
posts.care: MEMBER-FACING. Speaks to people already in the room about the worship leader and about carrying the Spirit. A stranger hearing this is being addressed as an insider. Caption leads on the half that includes them; the in-group beat is softened. Post to the existing-audience feed or Stories if in doubt.
posts.quote: You can make all the difference in this church if you determine to. You are the one that is carrying the Spirit.
posts.onscreen: "You bring more into a room" → "than you know."

captions.instagram:
Most of us walk into a room waiting for someone else to make it good.

The person at the front. The one with the microphone. Somebody more qualified, more sorted, further along than we are. We take a seat near the back and wait to be moved.

He turns that around gently. Whoever is leading will do their part, he says, but you brought something in with you. The room is different because you are in it.

He is talking about church, and it is just as true of a workplace, a family, a Tuesday evening with people you love. You are not audience. You never were.

Save this as a gentle nudge.

🎬 From "Enter Into The Kingdom" — Rev Ifeayinchukwu Obi. Full sermon on YouTube (search Calvary Hephzibah).

posts.title: What The King Asks
posts.quote: It's only looking back that you will see God. Not when you're in that situation.

captions.instagram:
Your boss asks you to lie. A small one. Nobody gets hurt, and everyone else has already said yes.

What struck me is that he did not pretend saying no is free. He said out loud that you might lose the job. That you might not have the school fees. He let the cost stand there without rushing past it.

And then the line that has stayed with me since Sunday: it is only looking back that you will see God. Not while you are standing in it.

Which is the hard part, isn't it. The clarity comes later. The decision comes now, in the dark, on what you know about who He is rather than what you can see.

If you are weighing something up this week, swipe through slowly.

🎬 From "Enter Into The Kingdom" — Rev Ifeayinchukwu Obi. Full sermon on YouTube (search Calvary Hephzibah).

posts.title: Treasure In A Field
posts.quote: For joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.

captions.instagram:
A man is digging in a field that is not his, and he finds treasure.

So he covers it back over. Goes home. Sells the lot. Comes back and buys one field that looks exactly like every other field on that road.

The word Jesus uses about him is joy. Not duty. Not sacrifice. He was glad to do it, because he had seen what was in the ground and nobody else had.

Then there is the other man in the story, rich and religious, told the same thing and walking away sorrowful. Same price. Opposite response. The difference was not courage or character. It was what each of them could see.

One saw what he was getting. The other only saw what he was giving up.

Most of us have been both. Swipe through and sit with which one today.

🎬 From "Enter Into The Kingdom" — Rev Ifeayinchukwu Obi. Full sermon on YouTube (search Calvary Hephzibah).

posts.title: Change Your Mind
posts.quote: I stopped walking in the wilderness of Christianity.

captions.instagram:
"Repent" is a word most people have only ever heard shouted.

So it arrives sounding like a verdict. Somebody has already decided what you are, and all that is left is to agree.

It means change your mind. That is the whole word. Think differently about who is running your life.

He knows the day he did it. 27 July 1987. And his phrase for what he walked out of has stayed with me: the wilderness of Christianity. Present every Sunday. Never actually decided anything.

You can change your mind today, quietly, where you are, without telling a soul.

And if you would rather not do it on your own, we gather Sundays at 11 in Manchester. No rush. Come as you are, and stay as long as you like.

🎬 From "Enter Into The Kingdom" — Rev Ifeayinchukwu Obi. Full sermon on YouTube (search Calvary Hephzibah).
